audience.primary: SME founders, CFOs, and finance leads at importers/exporters/payroll/B2B-payments/remittance companies operating in emerging markets with volatile currencies
segments: Importers paying USD invoices from local currency in Ghana, Nigeria, Kenya, Egypt
Exporters receiving USD and converting to local currency in Tanzania, Uganda, Argentina, Turkey
Payroll providers paying out in local currency on USD-denominated contracts
Remittance corridor operators bridging USDC inflows to local-currency payouts
B2B payment companies looking to add an FX-hedge revenue line for their merchants

content.headline: Insurance for currency fluctuation.
content.subheadline: Pay a small premium. Keep your working capital. Get paid out when the rate moves against you.
content.script: Your currency just dropped 12% overnight. Your $50,000 invoice just lost $6,000 in value. Welcome to running a business in an emerging market. // Traditional FX hedging asks you to lock up 30 to 50 percent of the notional, with a $100,000 minimum. If you're an SME, you can't afford that. So you don't hedge. And you eat the loss. // BlockFinaX is different. Pay a small premium, like insurance. Keep your working capital. If the rate moves against you, the smart contract pays you out automatically. No claim forms. No broker. Just instant settlement. // Backed by 22 years of FX data. 84 supported pairs. $1,000 minimum. 1 to 3 percent premium. // Stop absorbing FX losses. Start hedging like a Fortune 500.

scenes.text:
Your currency just dropped 12% overnight.
Your $50,000 invoice just lost $6,000.
scenes.voiceover: Your currency just dropped 12% overnight. Your $50,000 invoice just lost $6,000 in value. Welcome to running a business in an emerging market.
bRoll: Vertical: full-bleed deep-navy hero gradient. Large mono-typeface 'USD/GHS' ticker animating from 11.40 → 12.77 with a red downward arrow over the second number.
Bottom third: the dollar value '$50,000' typed in Inter 700, then morphing to '$50,000 → $44,000' with the delta '−$6,000' highlighted in dangerRed.
Subtle screen shake at the moment the rate jumps; a soft red glow vignette pulses once and recedes.
Avoid: globes, world maps, stacks-of-cash imagery.
scenes.notes: Hook is purely numeric — no narration text on screen. Let the typography + tickers do the work. Music: low confident drone enters at 0:01.

scenes.text:
Traditional FX hedging:
30–50% collateral lockup.
$100,000 minimums.
So you don't hedge. You eat the loss.
scenes.voiceover: Traditional FX hedging asks you to lock up 30 to 50 percent of the notional, with a $100,000 minimum. If you're an SME, you can't afford that. So you don't hedge. And you eat the loss.
bRoll: Split-screen card layout. Left card (white-on-charcoal) labelled 'TRADITIONAL' shows two big mono callouts: '30–50%' (collateral) and '$100,000' (minimum). Each renders with a heavy lock-icon glyph beside it.
After 2 seconds the left card fades to 50% opacity and a translucent red 'LOCKED' diagonal stamp appears across it — the 'SME can't access this' beat.
Right side remains empty/dark — the implicit promise that BlockFinaX will fill it.
Music: low rumble, slight tension build.
scenes.notes: This is the only beat where we explicitly call out the competition. Stay factual — no name-and-shame.

scenes.text:
BlockFinaX:
Pay a small premium. Keep your working capital.
Rate moves against you? Smart contract pays you out automatically.
scenes.voiceover: BlockFinaX is different. Pay a small premium, like insurance. Keep your working capital. If the rate moves against you, the smart contract pays you out automatically. No claim forms. No broker. Just instant settlement.
bRoll: Music shifts — tension resolves into a confident swell. Background gradient brightens to the brand hero (radial ellipse from #2e5bba → #1a4480 → #0f2744).
BlockFinaX hexagon logo enters from center, scaling up with a subtle blue glow accent matching the website hero.
Three on-screen data callouts in JetBrains Mono drop in stagger-fade: '1.7% premium' / '0% collateral' / 'auto-settled'.

Animated number ticker resolves to the AGAINST-YOU rate (12.50) hitting the configured cap, then a horizontal payout bar fills left-to-right with '+$87.72' counting up — a literal payout-in-real-time visual.
Avoid: anything that looks like a crypto-bro 'coin flying' animation. The vibe is Stripe's payments-flow microscale, not yieldfarm.
scenes.notes: This is the longest beat. Voiceover pacing should match the three callouts (one per ~2.5s) and end on 'instant settlement' as the payout bar completes.

scenes.text: 22 years of FX data · 84 supported pairs · $1,000 minimum · 1–3% premium.
scenes.voiceover: Backed by 22 years of FX data. 84 supported pairs. $1,000 minimum. 1 to 3 percent premium.
bRoll: 4-stat strip mirroring the website's stats section. Each cell: large mono number on top (e.g. '22+' in Inter 700, '84', '$1K', '1–3%') with a small Inter 500 caption below in skyText color.

Quick 1-line code snippet at the bottom in JetBrains Mono, dimmed but legible: POST https://api.blockfinax.com/v1/pricing/quote → 200 OK · $17.41 premium. Establishes 'this is a real API, not a deck'.
Music holds the resolved confident chord.
scenes.notes: Numbers should feel auditable, not marketing-fluff. The API line is the integrator wink — most viewers won't read it, but the right viewer (a founder/CFO who's considering integrating) will.

scenes.voiceover: Stop absorbing FX losses. Start hedging like a Fortune 500.
bRoll: Full-bleed brand-navy hero gradient.
Centered: BlockFinaX hexagon logomark (large, mark-only), then the tagline 'Stop absorbing FX losses. Start hedging like a Fortune 500.' typed in Inter 700.
URL chip below in JetBrains Mono on a translucent white pill: 'docs.blockfinax.com'.
Music resolves on a single sustained low chord that decays into silence on the last frame.
scenes.notes: Keep the URL in mono so it's instantly readable and 'API-able-feeling'. Logomark only (no wordmark) — the BlockFinaX text is in the tagline above.

music.mood: Trailer-house, deep + confident, slightly tense in hook/problem beats then resolving on the solution. Low bass drone with a single confident swell on the brand-reveal. Not bombastic — closer to a Stripe product launch than a movie trailer. Suggested licensing sources: Musicbed 'Cinematic Tension → Resolution' category, Artlist 'Inspiring Corporate' deep variants, or Epidemic Sound 'Trailer / Modern Cinematic' searches with BPM 70–90.

sfx.description: Subtle low-thud + slight digital glitch the moment the USD/GHS ticker jumps. Should feel like a market alert, not a horror sting.
Mechanical stamp/lock sound when the red LOCKED stamp lands on the traditional-hedging card.
Rising bright synth tail as the payout bar fills and the +$87.72 counter ticks up. Confident, not celebratory.
One soft 'whoosh-into-place' tick as the hexagon logo lands on the CTA frame.
